title: A Member's Right to a Second Look at a Denied Drug Coverage Determination
content:
A member of a Ridgecrest RxSecure stand-alone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan, their prescriber, or someone they have appointed in writing may ask the plan to look again at a denied drug coverage determination.

## The two conditions on a filing

1. **In time.** The plan receives the redetermination no later than the last day of the filing window counted from the date of the denial notice. Calendar days are counted from the day after that notice date, every day of the week counts, a redetermination received on the final day of the window is in time, and full 24-hour periods are never used in place of calendar days.
2. **Properly brought.** Where someone other than the member is filing, a valid appointment of representative form is on file, or the appointment is not required because the filer is the member's prescriber.

| Who is filing | Whether an appointment form must be on file |
| --- | --- |
| The member themselves | not required |
| The member's prescriber | not required, because Medicare treats the prescriber as able to act for the member on drug coverage |
| Anyone else acting for the member | required, and valid |

## A filing that arrives late

A redetermination received after the last day of the filing window is accepted only where good cause is shown, and then only inside the good-cause extension of the plan held; otherwise it is dismissed as filed after the window, with the reason explained.

## A filing that names no decision

The redetermination names the single denial it is filed against. One that names none is held while the plan asks the member which decision they mean, and is never dismissed for that reason alone.

## Where the denial is upheld

Where the plan upholds the denial the case goes to the independent review entity, and the member is told how and by when to take it further.
